subject: Geo-specific compensation adjustments for offers (US / EU / APAC) - approval request
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Geo-specific compensation adjustments for offers (US / EU / APAC) - approval request

Team —

We have a couple of active offers (including Sam Park, linked below) where location is driving a lot of back-and-forth. Recruiting is asking for a consistent rule-set we can apply for remote hires so we stop doing one-off approvals. I’ve attached a draft spreadsheet with proposed multipliers and an updated offer template covering US / EU / APAC.

High-level ask: sign off on a policy we can apply to offer letters this week (ideally before EOD Wed) so recruiting can finalize comp and close candidates.

Proposal (short):
- Keep Redwood bands as the baseline (band midpoints unchanged).
- Apply a regional multiplier to the band midpoint based on candidate location (examples below).
  - US (baseline): 1.00
  - EU (western Europe average): 0.98
  - APAC (mixed): 0.85
- Add a COLA (cost-of-living allowance) for specific high-cost cities (discretionary up to 7% of base): London, Singapore, San Francisco metro.
- Role exceptions: quota-bearing sales roles and highly senior ICs can be market-benchmarked and require a one-line approval from the hiring manager + VP (workflow stays as is).

Why this approach? It keeps band integrity while acknowledging geo variance; COLA preserves fairness for specific high-cost locales without creating dozens of localized bands. I’ve flagged Sam Park (candidate) in the spreadsheet — he’s remote and asked for London parity; his role is IC-level.

Please reply with: approve / approve with edits / need a quick call. I’d like clarity on EU vs UK (post-Brexit differences) and on whether we should apply state-level COLA within the US.

Attachments: geo_comp_adjustments_draft_v2.xlsx; offer-template-US-EU-APAC.docx

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Talent Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Geo-specific compensation adjustments for offers (US / EU / APAC) - approval request

Laura —

Thanks for pulling this together. Quick thoughts from People + Recruiting:

- Overall approach: approve in principle. Keeps bands consistent and reduces admin burden.
- EU vs UK: recommend separate multipliers for UK (London) vs continental EU given persistent premium in London; see vendor note below (I looped in Elena for benchmarking numbers).
- US internal variance: for now let's keep a single US baseline and use a small state-level COLA for high-cost states (CA, NY, MA) capped at 5% unless VP approval. That keeps the offer process fast.
- Senior hires (L5+ / Director): market exceptions as noted — require VP signoff and override reason on the offer doc.

Specific ask for Sam Park: he’s asking for London parity. If we treat London as a COLA city (up to 7%) + UK multiplier, his adjusted offer would fall within the recommended band. I’m OK pushing final offer with that if leadership signs off.

Proposed next step:
- Accept the attached multipliers spreadsheet with the UK split and a US state-COLA cap of 5%.
- If approved, I’ll update the offer templates and notify recruiting to proceed.

Elena — would appreciate the benchmarking numbers to finalize the recommended multipliers.

-Neha

Hi all —

Attached is a quick city/country benchmark summary based on the last 12 months of offers across our tech customers (summary CSV included in the attachment). Key takeaways:

- London (City): ~1.05 vs Redwood US baseline for comparable IC roles (high market premium).
- UK (rest): ~0.98-1.00 depending on role/experience.
- Germany (Berlin/Munich): ~0.98 overall.
- Netherlands (Amsterdam): ~1.02.
- Singapore: ~1.10 (notable premium for tech roles).
- India (Bengaluru/Delhi): ~0.60-0.70 (large gap vs US).

Notes:
- These are market medians; recommended approach is to use a regional multiplier table + city-level COLA for outlier metros.
- For quota-bearing sales roles we see significantly higher premiums in EMEA and APAC; recommend handling as exceptions rather than baking into bands.

Attachment: compbench_city_medians_Mar2026.csv

Happy to hop on 20–30 min to run through the sheet if useful.

—Elena

Thanks — I reviewed the draft and Elena’s benchmarks. Approve the policy with these operational guardrails: 

- Apply the regional multipliers as a baseline (US=1.00; EU baseline 0.98; APAC 0.85) and allow city-level COLA for London, Singapore, and SF up to 7%.
- US state COLA: implement a capped list (CA, NY, MA) at 5% — recruiting to flag if candidate is in-state vs remote-to-state.
- Sales & senior execs: market exceptions allowed but must include a short justification and VP signoff; recruiting should attach market comps when asking for an exception.
- For hire close velocity: recruiting can approve offers within band + COLA cap without further approvals. Anything above COLA caps or outside band requires VP approval.

Sam Park: approve moving forward with an offer using UK multiplier + London COLA capped at 7% (send final offer amplitude to me and Vivek before sending).

Laura - please publish final wording and update the offer-template document. Neha - deploy to hiring workflow and flag in Greenhouse (HR-REQ-2413).

Marcus
